storyline.label: Skill Evolution
storyline.latest_title: EvoGuard: Mitigating Degradation in Online Skill Evolution

prior_narrative.tldr: EvoSkill v2 (Oct 19) evolves agent skills, meaning instructions, without touching the model or harness. A Oct 26 paper extended this to coding agents with hierarchical skills.
prior_narrative.whats_new: ScienceCUA (Nov 2) builds skills from software manuals and web pages and refines them from execution feedback for scientific computer-use agents.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Skills are editable text, so agent behavior can improve without retraining; the open issue is whether evolved skills transfer across tasks and repos.

beats.headline: EvoSkill v2: a three-agent system that edits skills
Hierarchical skills separate reusable experience from repo-specific context
ScienceCUA builds skills from manuals and evolves them by execution

open_questions: Do evolved skills hold up on tasks and repositories outside their training benchmark?
Does skill evolution beat hand-written skills on a shared benchmark?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Version agent skills like code and keep a grader or benchmark, since evolution loops need a measurable signal to accept edits.
